tone_statements.citation: Ferlus, Michel. 2004. The origin of tones in Viet-Muong. In Somsonge Burusphat (ed.), Papers from the Eleventh Annual Conference of the Southeast Asian Linguistics Society 2001, 297-313. Tempe, Arizona: Arizona State University Programme for Southeast Asian Studies Monograph Series Press. Open copies:http://sealang.net/sala/archives/pdf8/ferlus2004origin.pdf; HAL halshs-00927222.
tone_statements.quote: The relative chronology of these two major phenomena for each language led to different types of tone systems (Ferlus 1998a). + If the devoicing of plosive initials took place after the complete loss of the two laryngeal features -? and -h, then the language developed a six-tone basic system as in northern VM languages (Vietnamese, Mudng, Th). * If the devoicing took place after the change of the laryngeal constriction -?, while final spirant -h was still preserved, then the language developed a four-tone basic system as in southern VM languages (Maleng, Arem, Säch/Ruc, Thavung).
tone_statements.locator: pp. 298-299, section 3 'Tonogenesis in Viet-Muong': the sentence 'The relative chronology.. (Ferlus 1998a).' closes p. 298; the two bulleted cases naming '(Vietnamese, Mường, Thổ)' and '(Maleng, Arem, Sách/Rục, Thavung)' open p. 299
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Thổ = northern Viet-Muong six-tone basic type (3 categories from -ø/-ʔ/-h × 2 registers from initial devoicing), like Vietnamese and Mường.

tone_statements.citation: Ferlus, Michel. 1998. Les systèmes de tons dans les langues viet-muong. Diachronica 15(1): 1-27. doi:10.1075/dia.15.1.02fer. Author's open copy: HAL halshs-00922841 (https://shs.hal.science/halshs-00922841v1/file/Ferlus1998_SystemesTonsVM.pdf).
tone_statements.quote: Les langues viet-muong offrent un large éventail de systèmes tonals, de quatre à six tons, provenant tous de deux systèmes antérieurs de base: l'un à six tons et l'autre à quatre tons où le -h est préservé. Le vietnamien, le mường et le cuối sont représentatifs d'un pur système à six tons dans leur définition la plus classique.
tone_statements.translation: The Viet-Muong languages offer a wide range of tone systems, from four to six tones, all deriving from two earlier basic systems: one with six tones and the other with four tones in which -h is preserved. Vietnamese, Mường and Cuối are representative of a pure six-tone system in its most classic definition.
tone_statements.locator: author's abstract on the HAL record halshs-00922841 (not the article text)
tone_statements.summary: Cuối (Thổ): classic six-tone Vietic system (per abstract).

sources.citation: Nguyễn Hữu Hoành, Bùi Thị Ngọc Anh & Hoàng Ngọc Tuệ. 2022. A Cuoi Language Description and Extensive Glossary. JSEALS Special Publication 10. Honolulu: University of Hawai'i Press. 122 pp.http://hdl.handle.net/10524/52504
sources.note: Silent on stress. Section 3 'Phonological summary' (pp. 4-10, Tan Hop Cuoi) covers syllable structure C1(C2)V(C3)+T, onsets, vowels, codas and five tones (35, 53, 24, 31ʔ, 44ʔ); the words 'stress', 'accent', 'prominence' do not occur anywhere in the 128-page PDF (only 'phrasal intonation' once, in the syntax chapter, p. 21); no stress marks in any transcription. Describes Cuoi as 'an isolating and monosyllabic language' in which 'syllables.. are both morphemes and single words' (p. 4).

sources.citation: Nguyễn Hữu Hoành & Nguyễn Văn Lợi. 2019. Tones in the Cuoi Language of Tan Ki District in Nghe An Province, Vietnam. Journal of the Southeast Asian Linguistics Society 12(1): lvii-lxvi.http://hdl.handle.net/10524/52449
sources.note: Silent on stress. Acoustic/phonological description of the Tan Hop (Tan Ky) tone system: seven surface tones (five on sonorant-final syllables, two on stopped syllables), analysable as five phonological tones; states 'Cuoi is a monosyllabic language, having only monosyllabic roots, not sesquisyllabic roots' (p. lvii). No mention of stress, accent or prominence.

sources.citation: Ferlus, Michel. 2001 [English version]. Hypercorrections in the Thổ dialect of Làng Lỡ (Nghệ An, Vietnam): an example of pitfalls for comparative linguistics. Quinzièmes Journées de Linguistique d'Asie Orientale, Paris, June 2001. HAL halshs-01128106.
sources.note: Silent on stress. Gives the Làng Lỡ Thổ phoneme inventory and tone table (8 etymological tone categories, 1-6 on live syllables, 7-8 on stopped syllables, categories 5 and 6 merged; p. 4) and discusses spirants/hypercorrection. No mention of stress or accent.

sources.quote: The relative chronology of these two major phenomena for each language led to different types of tone systems (Ferlus 1998a). + If the devoicing of plosive initials took place after the complete loss of the two laryngeal features -? and -h, then the language developed a six-tone basic system as in northern VM languages (Vietnamese, Mudng, Th). * If the devoicing took place after the change of the laryngeal constriction -?, while final spirant -h was still preserved, then the language developed a four-tone basic system as in southern VM languages (Maleng, Arem, Säch/Ruc, Thavung).
sources.locator: pp. 298-299, section 3 'Tonogenesis in Viet-Muong': the sentence 'The relative chronology.. (Ferlus 1998a).' closes p. 298; the two bulleted cases naming '(Vietnamese, Mường, Thổ)' and '(Maleng, Arem, Sách/Rục, Thavung)' open p. 299
sources.note: Tonogenesis account for the whole Vietic group: tones arose from loss of final -ʔ and -h (three categories) plus devoicing of initials (register split). It places Thổ with Vietnamese and Mường in the northern type, where devoicing followed the complete loss of both laryngeal finals, giving a 'six-tone basic system' (southern Maleng/Arem/Sách-Rục/Thavung have the four-tone type with -h kept). No Thổ-specific tone values or tables; per-language systems are referred to Ferlus 1998a.

sources.note: Per the HAL abstract: Viet-Muong languages show tone systems of four to six tones deriving from two earlier basic systems (six-tone; four-tone with -h preserved); 'Le vietnamien, le mường et le cuối sont représentatifs d'un pur système à six tons dans leur définition la plus classique' — i.e. Cuối/Thổ has the classic six-tone (2 registers × 3 categories) Vietic system; the article presumably tabulates the Cuối system (not seen).
